title: IntentIR
description: Intent Intermediate Representation (Intent IR): a structured, schema-validated description of a user's intent that can be produced by a rule-based or LLM compiler and consumed by downstream capability routing.

intent_id.description: Stable unique identifier for this intent instance (e.g. a UUID or slug).

intent_revision.description: Monotonic revision of this intent; never an authorization grant.

original_expression.description: The original human or machine expression, preserved without interpretation.

state.description: Lifecycle state of the intent representation.

goal.description: Canonical goal the user wants to achieve (e.g. retrieve_financial_document).

domain.description: Functional domain the intent belongs to (e.g. banking, travel, email).

action.description: Verb describing the operation (e.g. retrieve, create, update, delete).

object.description: The entity the action applies to (e.g. account_statement, invoice, flight).

constraints.description: Structured constraints narrowing the intent (e.g. period, amount, filters).

preferences.description: Non-mandatory preferences used to rank otherwise suitable fulfilment paths.

context.description: Ambient context (channel, session, locale, prior turns) that informs execution.

desired_output.description: Requested output format or artifact (e.g. pdf, json, csv, text).

authority.description: Authorization/entitlement requirements needed to execute the intent.

disclosure.description: Data-disclosure and privacy requirements (what may be shared, with whom).

success_conditions.description: Explicit conditions that must hold for the intent to be considered fulfilled.

confidence.description: Compiler confidence in the parsed intent, 0.0 (none) to 1.0 (certain).

uncertainty.description: Explicit unresolved fields, ambiguity, or clarification requirements.

fulfillment.description: Fulfillment and assurance state; execution success alone is not fulfillment proof.

metadata.description: Free-form metadata (compiler version, timestamps, provenance, etc.).
